events.title: British Troops Burn Washington's Public Buildings
events.description: On the second day of the burning of Washington during the War of 1812, British troops set fire to the Library of Congress, the Treasury and the Department of War, along with other public buildings.
events.significance: The attack was one of the lowest points of the War of 1812 for the young United States. It is still the only time a foreign force has captured and occupied the American capital.

events.title: The National Park Service Is Created
events.description: President Woodrow Wilson signed the National Park Service Organic Act into law. It created a federal agency to manage America's growing network of national parks and monuments.
events.significance: The law committed the United States to protecting its natural and historic treasures for future generations. It shaped the national park system that millions of people visit today.

events.title: Leonard Bernstein Is Born
events.description: Leonard Bernstein was born in Lawrence, Massachusetts. He became a celebrated conductor, composer and pianist, and led the New York Philharmonic from 1958 to 1969.
events.significance: Bernstein was one of the most influential American musicians of the 20th century. He is best known for composing West Side Story and for bringing classical music to wide audiences.

events.title: Paris Is Liberated
events.description: German commander Dietrich von Choltitz surrendered Paris to Allied and Free French forces. He had disobeyed Hitler's orders to destroy the city.
events.significance: The liberation ended four years of Nazi occupation of the French capital. It also left Paris and its landmarks largely intact.

events.title: Voyager 2 Reaches Neptune
events.description: NASA's Voyager 2 spacecraft made its closest approach to Neptune, the most distant giant planet in our solar system.
events.significance: Voyager 2 remains the only spacecraft ever to visit Neptune. It gave us our first close-up look at the planet and its moons.
